newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca sees higher 1997 capital spend, R&D.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca sees higher 1997 capital spend, R&D.

text.p: British bioscience company Zeneca Group Plc said on Tuesday it expected its capital spending to rise above 400 million stg in 1997 as it increases its manufacturing capacity for new products.
Capital spending by Zeneca jumped 34 percent in 1996 to 379 million stg, chief executive David Barnes told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"In 1997 it will go up to over 400 million pounds," Barnes said. Barnes said research and development spending topped 600 million stg last year, adding "I'd expect to see that increase in 1997 by about 10 percent."

"In 1996 we essentially, through increased capital expenditure and R&D, invested one billion pounds in the medium and long term of the business while making record profits of one billion pounds, generating cash and having an ungeared balance sheet. That is a very solid performance," Barnes told Reuters.

The chief executive said spending on a raft of new products, including migraine drug Zomig and asthma drug Accolate, would continue to restrict pharmaceutical profit margins to around 30 percent "for most of this year", compared with the 32 percent levels achieved two years ago.
